title: Last-vertex simplex resolution preserves cocone spaces
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices, ordinary nerves, quasicategories, functor simplicial sets, constant diagrams and right-pinched Kan mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], with universes enlarged as necessary. For a small simplicial set $X$, let $\mathsf S(X)$ be the ordinary category whose objects are all simplices $\sigma:\Delta^n\to X$, including degenerate simplices, and whose morphisms $\sigma\to\tau$ are monotone maps $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ with $\tau\Delta(\alpha)=\sigma$; composition is composition of the monotone maps. Define $\ell_X:N(\mathsf S(X))\to X$ on a chain $\sigma_0\to\cdots\to\sigma_r$, with $\sigma_i:\Delta^{n_i}\to X$, by applying $\sigma_r$ to the simplex of $\Delta^{n_r}$ whose $i$th vertex is the image of $n_i$ under the composite $[n_i]\to[n_r]$. For every quasicategory $\mathcal E$, every map $p:X\to\mathcal E$ and every vertex $T\in\mathcal E$, restriction itself induces an equivalence of Kan complexes
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(X,\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta_XT)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(\mathsf S(X)),\mathcal E)}(p\ell_X,\Delta_{N(\mathsf S(X))}T).$$
No quasicategory hypothesis on $X$ and no colimit-existence hypothesis on $\mathcal E$ is imposed. The assertion includes $X=\varnothing$.
